hooks.command: jq -c 'if (.tool_input.subagent_type // "") == "fork" then empty elif ((.tool_input.model // "") | length) == 0 then {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:"Agent dispatch has no `model` set. Omitting it is not a neutral default - the subagent INHERITS the session model, so a premium session silently spawns premium agents. Set model explicitly: haiku for mechanical work (extraction, pattern-following edits, structured search), sonnet for judgement work (multi-file reasoning, convention-holding prose), opus for a CODE REVIEW - that tier is standing for reviews and is not asked about, see CLAUDE.md - A review runs on opus. See CLAUDE.md - Subagent dispatch."}} elif (((.tool_input.description // "") | ascii_downcase) | test("review")) then empty elif ((.tool_input.isolation // "") != "worktree") then {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:"Agent dispatch does not set isolation to worktree. Every subagent that WRITES works in its own worktree, never the session clone: the dispatcher opens and closes it, the agent stays in the path it is given, runs no git, and never commits. A premium-model authorisation grants a model tier, not an isolation exemption. Forks and code reviews are the carve-outs - a review writes nothing, so it reads the session tree directly and gets no worktree. See CLAUDE.md - Subagent dispatch."}} elif ((.tool_input.model // "") | ascii_downcase | test("opus|fable")) then {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:("Agent dispatch requests the premium model \"" + (.tool_input.model) + "\". Per CLAUDE.md, opus/fable are forbidden for subagents unless you explicitly asked for that tier - EXCEPT a code review, which is standing on opus and passes without asking. Approve only if you asked for this tier.")}} else empty end'
